doc.title: Ruthie Foster interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 28, 2023

title: Spiritual but not religious music; Samantha Banks's 'spirit music'
summary: Her music is about spirit rather than religion, as drummer Samantha Banks used to say.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: Can your music be spiritual but not necessarily religious?

Um hum. That’s exactly what I feel that my music is and that’s where I feel comfortable where it is about spirit, very spiritual. And not necessarily about any particular religion. I know a lot of people do take my songs and they’ve been recorded in churches and sung still in church choirs and college choirs and I think that’s great. You know it’s more spirit. In fact my drummer, you might see there’s a picture, that’s me and her back there. It’s Samantha. She used to call it “spirit music” when people asked, “What type of music do you guys do?” And she says, “It’s spirit music.” Music that moves your spirit. And the
other thing she used to say when I would go out and do my own shows by myself, solo shows, and she would call and remind me, “You’ve got this girl, just go and make ‘em cry.”
